newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-CENTRAL BANK CHIEF SUPPORT MARKETS WATCHDOG.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-CENTRAL BANK CHIEF SUPPORT MARKETS WATCHDOG.

text.p: Central bank chief Einar Repshe on Wednesday said he backed the idea of one watchdog to police Latvia's emerging financial markets.
The idea of a single supervisory body has been floated by Finance Minister Robert Zile, who wants an institution along the line of Sweden.
"The bank in principle supoprts the idea of the creation of a single supervising institution," Repshe told a news conference.
"But I stress that firstly it should not happen in a hurry and second it has to be as good or better than the existing supervision of commercial banks," he added.
The central bank has considerably boosted its supervision of the country's banks since a crisis in 1995 over the collapse of what was once the largest bank, Banka Baltiya.
